messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a weird case in prod where a feature-flag rollback happened but our metrics and the console audit stream show no rollback event. app-team reported traffic shifted back but there's no config-change entry tied to the request-id :thinking:

alex: oh no. which flag / route? any trace ids from the app logs we can correlate? :eyes:

maria: flag: enable_new_routing (route-priority). Happened around 10:24 UTC. App logs show request-id `req-9f3b` and an internal note `applied fallback route`. No `config.apply` event in `console-audit-v2`.

lee: could be two possibilities: (1) a direct DB toggle (bypassing the service) or (2) a dry-run shadow that mutated local runtime but didn't persist. Did the deploy bot run around then? ops-bot:deploy-log? :mag:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: No deployments in prod during 10:00-10:30 UTC. Canary rollouts: none.

alex: ok. can you run a quick query on the config-snapshot table and the audit log for that window? sample SQL: ```SELECT id, flag_name, change_type, actor, metadata FROM console_audit WHERE flag_name='enable_new_routing' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-11-18T10:00:00Z' AND '2025-11-18T10:30:00Z' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;```

maria: ran it — nothing returned. snapshot table shows a change in the value at 10:23:45 but snapshot.source = 'runtime-cache' and snapshot.tx_id is null. So it looks like the runtime mutated but the control-plane didn't record a transaction.

lee: that indicates an agent-level change (agent synced local override) or an ephemeral apply path. Are we still honoring the runtime-config apply-without-transaction API? We added that as an escape hatch for oncall in emergencies but it should emit an audit event.

alex: right — the API path `POST /v1/flags/:name/apply?persist=false` was meant to not persist but should still write a zero-footprint audit entry: `{actor: 'operator', via: 'runtime-api', tx_id: generated}`. Looks like the audit write failed intermittently. Check the control-plane logs for ephemeral-audit failures. Query idea: ```grep "ephemeral-audit" /var/log/control-plane/* | jq -r '.message' | grep "enable_new_routing"```

maria: control-plane logs show `ephemeral-audit: write failed - timeout` at 10:23:46 and a retry that returned 504, then the apply returned 200 to the caller. So we have a gap: runtime applied, audit write timed out and wasn't retried durably.

lee: ugh. that's a bug. Two follow-ups: (A) ensure the runtime-api returns 5xx when audit fails to force caller to retry (or mark as partial and enqueue durable write), (B) add a reconciliation job to compare runtime snapshots to control-plane state and emit missing audit items.

alex: also need console UX: when reconciliation detects a runtime-only change, present it as `Unrecorded runtime mutation — requires operator ack` with a direct "create audit record" button that attaches evidence (request ids, logs). Saves ops from hunting.

maria: agreed. For now I'll open a quick incident card and add the affected request-ids. Short-term mitigation: flip the runtime-api to a fail-closed behavior for audit writes. Who can own the change?

lee: I'll take the backend fix (make audit write sync-durable or fail-closed). Timeline: patch + rollout to control-plane staging in 4h, canary to prod overnight.

alex: I'll add the console UX bit to a small ticket (devex) — mockup + API to create missing audit records based on evidence. Also add telemetry: a gauge `runtime_unrecorded_changes_total` and an alert when >0 in 5m for any tenant. Query proto: ```sum by(tenant) (increase(runtime_unrecorded_changes_total[5m])) > 0```

maria: sounds good. For the incident card: summary "runtime-only flag mutation -> missing audit event"; initial owner maria, backend owner lee, devex alex.

devex-bot: Created incident INC-2025-341 in #incidents with priority P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-341

maria: thanks. small ask — can we also log the audit write request-id into the runtime apply response header (X-Audit-Req) so callers can correlate? If the write times out, runtime should include a `retry-token` that the console button uses to re-submit evidence.

alex: yep that fits the UX. I'll add `X-Audit-Req` and `X-Audit-Retry` headers to the runtime-api response and update the SDKs.

lee: one more: add a nightly reconciliation job that emits telemetry of drift reasons (agent-override, persisted-mismatch, missing-audit). We'll use that to prioritize.

maria: perfect. I'll add the notes to the incident and ping the app-team to check if they saw user-visible errors. Closing out here unless anyone has other quick ideas :slightly_smiling_face:

alex: nothing else. thanks for catching this, maria :thumbsup:

lee: thanks — tracking in the incident.

ops-bot: Note: rollout paused was not triggered by this — just FYI.
